h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A 0->3 identity turns the deep 0->1->2->3 chain into a residual branch that is easier to optimise, so adding a 3x3 conv on edge 2 pays off more.
With an identity shortcut into node 3, a conv on the final deep edge only has to learn a residual refinement, which raises its marginal value.
A strong conv on the sibling input to node 3 dominates the sum, so the accuracy penalty for pooling edge 4 shrinks.
A conv on the direct 0->3 edge carries discriminative features into node 3, which makes pooling edge 4 comparatively cheap.
Without edge 5, node 3 is fed only by edges 3 and 4, so deleting the 0->3 edge removes half the output inputs and risks a near-dead cell.
Node 2 still receives a strong learned transform through edge 2, so pruning the 0->2 edge costs little.
When node 2 feeds a 3x3 conv into the output, impoverishing node 2's inputs degrades an important branch.
With a 3x3 conv heading the deep path, an input-to-output identity forms a ResNet-style block with better gradient flow.
If node 3 already receives a near-identity of early features via edge 4, a second identity over-weights raw features and adds little.
A strong 3x3 conv on edge 4 dominates node 3, so pooling edge 5 is diluted and less harmful.
